quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: Proper riding clothing provides all of the following except:

options.text: Comfort.
Protection in a crash.
Protection from cold weather.
Discomfort.

questions.correctAnswerText: Discomfort.
questions.explanation: Proper riding clothing protects you from injury in a crash. It also protects you from weather and common discomforts like heat and cold.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to go.
Press the handlebar grip in the opposite direction you want to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to go.
questions.explanation: To swerve and avoid a hazard, press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn. To swerve left, press the left grip, then the right to straighten. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left to straighten.

questions.question: If a passing vehicle creates a wind blast, you have the most room to recover if you ride:

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
In the center of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane gives you the most space to adjust if a wind blast pushes your motorcycle off balance.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to hazards and changing road conditions ahead.

questions.question: To carry a passenger, you may need to adjust all of the following except:

options.text: Tire pressure.
Mirror positions.
Headlight position.
Brake light position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake light position.
questions.explanation: With a passenger, your motorcycle sits lower due to extra weight. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, headlight, and mirrors. The brake light position does not need adjustment.

questions.question: As weight shifts forward while you brake, you should:

options.text: Slowly increase pressure on the front brake.
Use more rear brake pressure.
Not worry. Weight shift will not affect your motorcycle.
Try to lock the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly increase pressure on the front brake.
questions.explanation: As you brake, gradually increase front brake pressure as the weight moves forward to the front tire. This helps you stop safely without locking the wheel.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is usually a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limit signs, are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while turning, you should:

options.text: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
Apply both brakes hard while leaning.
Apply only the rear brake.
Apply only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
questions.explanation: First straighten your motorcycle and square the handlebars, then stop. If you cannot straighten the motorcycle, apply brakes slowly and gradually while reducing your lean angle, then increase brake pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: If the throttle gets stuck, you should:

options.text: Jump off the motorcycle.
Apply the brakes.
Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Do not try to twist the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: If your throttle gets stuck, twist it back and forth to free it. If this does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: You can discourage other vehicles from sharing your lane by:

options.text: Riding on the left side of the lane.
Riding in the center of the lane.
Making angry gestures at other drivers.
Riding in a zigzag pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride more slowly than normal.
Start slowing down earlier than normal.
Increase your following distance.
Avoid talking to your passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking to your passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. This makes it respond more slowly. With a passenger, ride slower, start slowing sooner, and increase your following distance. Always warn your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Kick the dog away.
Ride alongside the dog.
Stop until the dog loses interest.
Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Slow down and approach the dog. Then speed up and leave it behind. If you see a larger animal, brake and be ready to stop.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to drive, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Ask other friends to talk them out of driving.
Arrange different transportation for them.
Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
Slow down their drinking pace.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: You can prevent drunk driving by arranging other transportation, involving them in other activities to slow their drinking, finding excuses to keep them from leaving until sober, and asking friends to help you intervene together.

questions.question: When planning a long group ride, which idea should you avoid?

options.text: Plan travel distance based on the least experienced rider.
Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
Place inexperienced riders behind the leaders.
Use a staggered riding formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
questions.explanation: Plan trip distance based on the least experienced rider. Take regular breaks to reduce fatigue. Place inexperienced riders behind the leader so they can be watched. Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve:

options.text: Speeds greater than 35 mph.
Riding at night.
Worn tires.
Riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders who have owned their motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which should you NOT tell them to do?

options.text: Get on after you start the engine.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Talk whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should avoid talking or moving unnecessarily so you can focus on riding. Passengers should get on only after the engine starts. They should sit forward without crowding you and hold on firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: At speeds greater than 55 mph.
After riding for several hours.
On short trips.
On long trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles at speeds slower than 30 mph.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while riding, you should:

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Speed up.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has oil and is slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars when it rains. Slow down on wet surfaces.

questions.question: The center of a lane:

options.text: Is always the best place for a motorcycle.
Has oil and grease but is usually safe for riding.
Has oil and grease and is never safe for riding.
Is the smoothest part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has oil and grease but is usually safe for riding.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of the lane. Unless the road is wet, this area usually has enough grip for safe riding. Avoid large oil and grease buildups, often found at busy intersections or toll booths.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: At high speeds.
After riding for a long time.
Far from home.
On short trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips less than five miles long at speeds slower than 30 mph.

questions.question: The middle of the lane usually has an oily strip. What should you do?

options.text: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining.
Ride only on the oily strip because it gives better grip.
Avoid the entire center of the lane.
Do not worry about oil or other items in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars and trucks builds up in the center of each lane. When the road is dry, this strip usually still has enough grip for a motorcycle. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride around it and still stay in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the brake until the rear tire grips again, then brake again.
Release the brake and use only the front brake.
Keep the brake locked until the motorcycle stops.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until the motorcycle stops.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while braking, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until you come to a complete stop.

questions.question: How can you reduce the time you need to react to a hazard?

options.text: Always ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready over the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready over the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hands ready over the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Do not swerve and only use the front brake to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a collision, do these actions separately, not at the same time. Braking while swerving may cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for riding a motorcycle?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The center of the lane
The right side of the lane
The best position depends on the riding conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The best position depends on the riding conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best and no position should always be avoided. Choose a lane position that matches your riding conditions. This helps you keep safe distance and stay visible to other drivers.
